body: Thanks for the bug report! This will be fixed in 2.5.1 (and available in the first prerelease build--which has not shipped to NuGet yet--if you want to test it early).

@bradwilson do you have a timeline on 2.5.1 (or even a prerelease to test) I am facing the same bug. I have reverted for the moment.

Thank you very much for fixing though
There will be a prerelease this week
Wow I blinked and there was a reply. Thanks
You caught me on my phone and the GitHub app notification popped up 😂

I can confirm this was fixed with 2.5.1-pre.12, thank you for the fast prompt!
Wasted an hour trying to understand what i screwed with my code 🤣

@bradwilson Thanks so much for all the hard work on xunit. I just ran into this issue myself when updating to `2.5.0` so eagerly watching for when 2.5.1 is released. Updated like 300 tests to use `Assert.Equivalent` but I will probably stay on `2.4.x` for now. Should have looked at the issues before all that work 🤦‍♂️

@Matthewsre You can try it right now with a 2.5.1 prerelease build on NuGet. (I am away from my coding computer for a while and cannot verify it myself). https://www.nuget.org/packages/xunit/2.5.1-pre.20

Also, if you want me to verify it, you need to provide a complete sample. The provided dictionary is not a complete test, just sample data. It's best for me not to have to guess what you're doing. 😄
@chotea No need for a new issue. I have a fix incoming.
